policy_title: Clean Air Act and Air Quality Agency
stated: Pass a Clean Air Act, based on World Health Organization guidelines, enforced by a new Air Quality Agency. Tackling air pollution and poor air quality in public buildings with a Clean Air Act.

source.quote: Pass a Clean Air Act, based on World Health Organization guidelines, enforced by a new Air Quality Agency. Tackling air pollution and poor air quality in public buildings with a Clean Air Act, as set out in chapter 12.

bearing_set.reason: Directly targets air pollution and air quality through binding legislation and a new enforcement agency, with WHO-guideline standards — a primary, non-negligible effect on clean environment.
Air quality has well-established causal links to respiratory and cardiovascular health outcomes; tighter standards would plausibly reduce disease burden and NHS demand materially.

membership_note: Two genuine bearings: O6 is the policy's direct target; O3 follows from the established health-burden evidence linking air pollution to NHS demand. Regulatory compliance costs on businesses (O13) and agency setup costs (O12) are real but too diffuse and small relative to overall economic activity to clear the non-negligible bar at this level of policy specification. O10 (personal liberty) is not materially engaged — the primary regulatory burden falls on emitters, not individual speech, bodily autonomy or privacy.
